```{r user_vars}

# get the datetime and set it to variable for inline printing
todays.date <- Sys.Date()
formatted.date <- format(todays.date, format="%B %d %Y")

# Import the config file
config.args <- read_yaml(params$config.args)

run_metrics_tables=TRUE
metrics.table.string <- config.args$analysis$part1$generate_metrics_tables

if (metrics.table.string == "FALSE"){
  run_metrics_tables=FALSE
}

cfg <- config.args
cfg.analysis <- cfg$analysis

p1  <- cfg.analysis$part1
p2 <- cfg.analysis$part2

################################################################################
# set project variables
################################################################################
part2.suffix <- p2$part2_suffix
analyst.name <- config.args$project$`analyst-name`
formatted.samples <- config.args$project$samples # Sanitized below
experiment.name = config.args$project$`project-name` 
project.description <- config.args$project$`project-decription`
dataset.path <- config.args$data$parent_directory_path
import.h5 <- config.args$data$`import-h5` # set to false if you want to import the matrix files
organism = config.args$project$organism
num.clusters <- config.args$analysis$part2$num_clusters

clustering.resolution <- p2$clustering_resolution
if (is.null(clustering.resolution) || identical(as.character(clustering.resolution), "None"))
  stop("clustering_resolution is not set in the config — run part 2b before part 3.")

################################################################################
# Set output directory paths
################################################################################

r.obj.loc <- config.args$data$`rds-file-path` # Output folder

# When trying different parameters in the analysis you can create
# alternate output files with this 'suffix' argument in the config
part1.suffix <- p1$part1_suffix

unfiltered.seurat.obj.file <- config.args$analysis$part1$unfiltered_seurat_obj_file
unfiltered.seurat.obj.file <- sub(".RDS", paste0(part1.suffix, ".RDS"), unfiltered.seurat.obj.file )
unfiltered.seurat.obj.path <- file.path(r.obj.loc, unfiltered.seurat.obj.file)

QC.tables.file <- p1$part1_report_tables_filename
QC.tables.file <-sub(".RData", paste0(part1.suffix, ".RData"), QC.tables.file)
QC.tables.path <-file.path(r.obj.loc, QC.tables.file)
part2.tables.path <- suffix_path(r.obj.loc, p2$part2_report_tables_filename, part2.suffix)


ggplot.directory.name <- p1$ggplot_dir
ggplot.directory <- file.path(r.obj.loc, ggplot.directory.name)

marker.gene.dir <- suffix_path(r.obj.loc, p2$marker_gene_dir, part2.suffix)

ids <- sanitize_sample_names(formatted.samples)
```

# Part 2: Integration, clustering, and differential expression

## Pre-integration UMAP

```{r pre-int_umap}
merged.umap.path <- file.path(ggplot.directory, "umap_merged_seruat_obj.png")

knitr::include_graphics(merged.umap.path)
```

### Post-integration UMAP

We integrate all of the samples together into a single object for comparison
of cell types across samples. Go [here](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/integration_introduction.html) to read more about single-cell integration. 

## Post-integration UMAP by sample

```{r post-int_umap}
integrated.umap.path <- file.path(ggplot.directory, "integrated_umap_by_sample.png")

knitr::include_graphics(integrated.umap.path)
```


### Clustering

To group cells into clusters, we scan a range of clustering resolutions (a resolution setting simply controls how finely the cells get divided: lower values yield fewer, broader clusters and higher values yield more, smaller ones). To choose among them, we measure cluster stability: at each resolution we repeatedly take a random 80% of the cells, re-cluster them, and check how consistently the same clusters reappear. Clusters that keep reforming under this resampling are treated as real structure, while ones that dissolve are a sign the data is being split too finely. 

We then automatically select the finest resolution whose clusters remain reliably reproducible, which gives us as much biological detail as the data can actually support without over-splitting. This is an objective starting point rather than a final answer: the "best" resolution is flexible, since neighboring values often give very similar results, and interpretation still depends on marker genes and biological context. In other words, this clustering is an educated guess that can be adjusted (clusters can be merged or split, or a different resolution chosen to generate more or fewer clusters, though the overall shape of the UMAPs won't change).


The plot below shows this stability at each resolution (higher is more stable), with the number of clusters labeled above each point. The pipeline selected the resolution marked in red: the finest one whose stability still clears the data-derived threshold shown in blue.

## Table of cells per cluster from each sample

```{r cluster_sample_table, results='asis'}

cluster.sample.df <- read.csv(file.path(r.obj.loc, "cells_perCluster_perSample.csv"),
                              row.names=1)
cluster.sample.df %>%
  kable(format = "latex",
        booktabs = TRUE,
        caption = "Cell counts per cluster per sample",
        longtable = FALSE,
        row.names = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"),
    font_size = 8
  ) %>%
  row_spec(0, angle = 45, font_size = 7) %>%
  row_spec(nrow(cluster.sample.df), bold = TRUE) %>%  # bold Total row
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) %>%                      # bold Cluster column
  column_spec(ncol(cluster.sample.df), bold = TRUE)    # bold Total column

# cluster.sample.df
```

## Marker genes

For each cluster, which genes are differentially expressed in that 
cluster compared to all other clusters combined?

```{r gene_feature, fig.width = 25, fig.height = 20}
assay.used <- "SCT"

# Cluster IDs come from the marker table 2b wrote, not 0:(num_clusters - 1):
# a cluster with no positive markers gets no figures (only.pos = TRUE), and IDs
# aren't guaranteed contiguous if clusters were filtered by hand.
marker.csv <- file.path(marker.gene.dir,
                        paste0("cluster_markers_", clustering.resolution, ".csv"))
if (!file.exists(marker.csv))
  stop("Marker table not found: ", marker.csv, " — run part 2b first.")
clusters.present <- sort(unique(read.csv(marker.csv)$cluster))

# Mirror the plot types 2b was configured to draw, so part 3 never asks for a
# panel that was never generated.
marker.plot.types <- p2$marker_plot_types %||% c("feat", "dot")

# One path per (cluster, kind), interleaved so each cluster's panels stay together.
figure.list <- unlist(lapply(clusters.present, function(cluster.num) {
  vapply(marker.plot.types,
         function(kind) marker_plot_path(ggplot.directory, cluster.num, kind,
                                         assay.used, part2.suffix),
         character(1))
}), use.names = FALSE)

absent <- figure.list[!file.exists(figure.list)]
if (length(absent))
  warning("Marker plots missing, omitted from the report: ",
          paste(basename(absent), collapse = ", "))
figure.list <- figure.list[file.exists(figure.list)]

if (length(figure.list) == 0) {
  cat("No marker gene plots were found in", ggplot.directory, "\n")
} else {
  knitr::include_graphics(figure.list)
}
```
